highlight.html: Quiet, subscriber-heavy week — event volume, thin qualification. 161 new contacts (136 subscribers + 24 on the qualified track), with 9 MQL+, 4 SQL+ and 3 opportunities. The new "State of AI in Australian Businesses" launch event drove 80 Facebook contacts but 0 MQL — pure top-of-funnel. DecidrOS added 3 MQL but no SQLs; all 4 SQL+ were Unassigned. The Facebook "AI Roadmap" demo campaign again converted 3/3 to MQL and produced the week's only marketing SQL (Will Patris) plus an opportunity (Paul Giordano); two more opps were sales-created in-CRM.

observations.html: Quiet week after a strong one. 24 qualified contacts, 9 MQL+, 4 SQL+ — down from Week 26's 38 MQL+ / 10 SQL+. Subscriber-heavy (136 of 161) top of funnel.

New "State of AI" launch event: 80 contacts, 0 MQL. The biggest volume driver ($3,203 Meta) produced zero near-term MQLs — expected for a launch/awareness event, but the downstream conversion is the thing to watch.

AI Roadmap still converts — but starving for audience. 3/3 MQL and the week's only marketing SQL (Will Patris) + an opp (Paul Giordano). Volume fell to 3 leads for $2,203 ($734/lead) — the audience is thinning; refresh creative/targeting to re-scale.
DecidrOS: 3 MQL, 0 SQL. No DecidrOS deals progressed to SQL this week. Watch whether these MQLs convert next week.
Product-tagging gap. All 4 SQL+ are Unassigned, including 2 clearly DecidrOS-intent AI Roadmap contacts (Will Patris, Paul Giordano). Tag product on the AI Roadmap lead form to fix attribution.
Paid media $10,131 — Meta $8,507 (84%), LinkedIn $1,178, Google $446. Blended $80 / paid lead. LinkedIn ran awareness only (0 MQL); Google brand-search only, 0 HubSpot contacts.
Low junk — 1 disqualified contact. Only one contact was disqualified this week (DecidrOS-tagged). Lead hygiene is healthy.
